cue: What's the extra December paycheck called?

es.meaning: The year-end bonus Mexican employers must pay by 20 December, by law at least fifteen days' wages. In a posada, 'aguinaldo' is also the small bag of candy and fruit handed to guests.
es.example: Con el aguinaldo vamos a comprar los regalos.
es.exampleTranslation: We'll buy the presents with the Christmas bonus.
es.regionNote: In Spain the equivalent is usually 'la paga extra' (one in summer, one at Christmas); 'aguinaldo' there leans toward a small tip or gift.

it.meaning: A thirteenth monthly salary paid to employees in December, on top of the twelve regular ones. It is part of the annual salary, spread across the year by contract, not a discretionary bonus.
it.example: Con la tredicesima ci paghiamo le vacanze di Natale.
it.exampleTranslation: The thirteenth-month pay covers our Christmas holiday.

bridge.note: Same December money, named from opposite ends. Spanish names it after the occasion: 'aguinaldo' is a Christmas gift, and the word still covers the candy bag at a posada. Italian names it by arithmetic: 'tredicesima' is simply the thirteenth month of pay. The Italian word says nothing about Christmas and the Spanish word says nothing about salary, so neither one translates the other literally.

interference.es_to_it: Asking an Italian about their 'aguinaldo' gets a blank look; the salary is 'la tredicesima', and a Christmas tip or gift is 'una mancia' or 'un regalo'.
interference.it_to_es: An Italian who calls the Mexican bonus 'el decimotercero' will be understood with effort; the word everyone uses is 'aguinaldo'.
